global: The bandits who haunt the pass beyond {town} grow bolder by the week, and the local garrison sleeps through it all.
Bread in {town} now costs more than a knight's oath, and I am told this is merely the beginning of the reckoning.
Ser {rival}'s levies trample every field they cross, yet no one dares name the debt they leave behind.
The wages set for guarding the caravans are a jest, and a poor one, fit only for a fool who has never ridden those roads.
I swore an oath to the house of {faction} long ago, yet their tariffs now shame every honest merchant on this road.
Four days I waited at the crossroads for an escort, and not a single sword came. Shameful, ser, truly shameful.
The smiths of {town} ask for silver as though iron were gold dust. I have never seen such greed in the market square.
Our ancestors fought the marsh raiders with pride, while today's guards haggle over their pay before they draw a blade.
Ser {rival} claims the eastern bridge by right of conquest, though honour would sooner see it burned than hoarded.
Tell me, friend, why a bandit lord in these hills can afford silk while my lands go hungry? Justice has grown thin.
